title: Mono part of affine-basis section resolution comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], V an affine open, and F,J integer-indexed complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose J is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and i:F → J is a quasi-isomorphism. For every affine W contained in V, assume all positive cohomology groups [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor] of each term of F, each differential cokernel of F, and each cohomology sheaf of F restricted to W vanish. For every integer n, the map H^n(Γ(V,F)) → H^n(Γ(V,J)) induced by i is a monomorphism of O_X(V)-modules. The section complexes are formed by termwise native module evaluation. Empty V is allowed; no boundedness or quasi-coherence is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08C2, lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-ss, singleton cover; Tag 071B, lemma-K-injective. Source TeX read in sandbox scratchpad/cohomology.tex.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-integer-section-acyclic-incoming-kernel-image at V, using the cokernel and homology vanishing hypotheses with W = V. This gives the first module-cohomology vanishing of the incoming kernel and image at degree n. No termwise vanishing or tower argument is used.

Apply lem-pc-short-complex-section-comparison to F.sc n. Its adjunction-normalized presheaf homology-to-sheaf-homology comparison is invertible after evaluation at V. The theorem is stated after forgetting scalars; the exact faithful module-to-group forgetful functor reflects its invertibility as a module map.

Prove naturality of the adjunction-normalized comparison for a map of short complexes: inverse sheafification homology comparison is natural, and the counit is natural. Applying the adjunction homEquiv gives the square for the section class map. Since i is a quasi-isomorphism, its map on sheaf homology is invertible, and so is its evaluation. The composite of the invertible source comparison and this evaluated map is therefore mono. By the square, the evaluated presheaf homology map followed by the target comparison is mono, so that presheaf homology map is mono. The target comparison need not be invertible.

Exact presheaf evaluation has a natural homology isomorphism. Conjugate the preceding mono through these isomorphisms to obtain the map on homology of termwise native module evaluation. This is definitionally the displayed resolution homology map. Zero complexes, empty opens and all integer degrees are included.

proof_origin.place: Direct cycle/opcycle dimension shifting followed by naturality of the existing short-complex section comparison; no inverse-limit tower.

theorem affineBasisSections_resolution_homology_mono
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (F J : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) [J.IsKInjective]
    (i : F ⟶ J) [QuasiIso i]
    (hterms : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((F.X n).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1)))
    (hcokernels : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((cokernel (F.d (n - 1) n)).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1)))
    (hhomology : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((F.homology n).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1))) (n : ℤ) :
    let S := SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (op V)
    letI : S.Additive := inferInstanceAs
      ((SheafOfModules.forget.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj (op V)).Additive)
    Mono (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      ((S.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map i) n)
